newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil steady despite crude.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil steady despite crude.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps were steady late afternoon on Wednesday despite further falls to crude values on top of a big overnight drop as the market looked to physical purchases by some traders for support, traders said.
"The market is holding up surprisingly well. I think it's because of the continued buying from some traders," one trader said.
June gas oil swaps were quoted at $24.80/$24.90 per barrel while July was at $24.70/$24.80, down 20 cents for the front month from Monday's quotes but unchanged from the morning, brokers said.
July was down 15 cents from Monday leading to a widening of the June/July time spread to 10 cents --a level that was traded on Tuesday.
July gas oil traded earlier in the day at $24.75 per barrel while July traded at $24.78, brokers said.
Traders said the market remains fundamentally bearish but the sustained support from two local traders and one Japanese traders has kept prices from falling further.
The three traders have in total bought over 22 million barrels of physical gas oil since March 3.
Traders said the market is reeling from distressed cargoes in China were up to four prompt cargoes are unsold.
Also the prompt overhang in the Singapore spot market has led to a 40 cents contango in the physical market between cargoes loading 15 days forward and those loading 30 days out.
On Tuesday a 150,000 barrel traded at $25.30 per barrel for June 29-July 3 lifting compared to offers at $24.90 for lifting June 19-23 lifting, traders said.
June fuel oil swaps were last quoted down about 50 cents per tonne at $100.25/$101.50 because of the big crude drop.
Overnight July Brent crude closed down 62 cents to $18.90 per barrel on the International Petroleum Exchange and was last traded down 14 cents to $18.76.
